name: Warp Factory Worker
description: Self-hosted worker for Warp Factories (oz-agent-worker), integrated with this box's local resources. Warp Factories is a cloud platform for running fleets of coding agents across your SDLC; the control plane (factories, runs, projects) is hosted by Warp, and this worker runs the actual agent tasks on your own infrastructure. It is a headless background daemon with no web UI: it mounts the host Docker socket so it can spawn task containers, and connects outbound over a WebSocket to Warp's Automation Platform. Out of the box it uses the Docker backend and a seeded worker.yaml that (a) points every agent harness at the local vLLM model (fable / Qwen3.8-27B) over the Tailscale IP, (b) mounts the Android SDK for Gradle builds, and (c) mounts Phone-Projects as the first project. It requires a Warp Enterprise plan and a self-hosted worker API key (wk-...) to authenticate; without a valid key it starts and retries the connection. The worker is open source and the image is pinned to a specific release tag.
short_desc: Self-hosted worker for Warp Factories cloud coding agents
author: Mohammad Reza Rastgoo

form_fields.label: Warp Self-Hosted Worker API Key
form_fields.hint: A self-hosted worker API key (starts with wk-) from your Warp Enterprise account. Required for the worker to authenticate to the Automation Platform.

form_fields.label: Worker ID
form_fields.hint: A stable identifier for this worker. Warp routes runs to workers by this id.

form_fields.label: Extra CLI Arguments (optional)
form_fields.hint: Any additional flags to pass to the oz-agent-worker binary, e.g. a path to a YAML config file.
